commands.review_summary:
The PR changes `src/infra/dispatch-wrapper-resolution.ts` so `flock` skips `--` after a lock target and `script` treats a consumed `--` as meaning there is no transcript file.

PR surface: Source +5. Total +5 across 1 file.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible: the PR head returns `commandIndex` after a consumed `--`, so `script -- echo hello` becomes `echo hello` in wrapper analysis even though the `script(1)` contract still requires a transcript file before a command. I did not run tests because this review is read-only.

target.title: fix(dispatch-wrapper): fix flock separator and script command detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two dispatch-wrapper resolution bugs:

1. **flock `--` separator**: `flock /tmp/lock -- echo hello` was not unwrapped because `--` was treated as an option-like token. Now skipped as the POSIX separator between lock target and command.

2. **script command detection**: `script -- echo hello` mislabeled `echo` as a transcript file. Now detects the `--` separator form (all tokens are command) vs. transcript-file form (first token after options is transcript, rest is command). Transcript-only invocations like `script -q /dev/null` stay blocked.

## Why This Change Was Made

- flock: detect `--` after lock target and skip past it
- script: check if `--` was consumed by the scanner to distinguish command-only from transcript-file forms

## User Impact

Fixes command execution analysis for `flock` and `script` invocations with `--` separator.

## Evidence

**Runtime terminal proof:**

![screenshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhangLei99586/openclaw/proof-screenshots/pr-98657-proof.png)

- `exec-wrapper-resolution.test.ts`: 132/132 passed ✅
- `exec-approvals-allow-always.test.ts`: 48/48 passed ✅
- flock -- + script -- verified at runtime on fix branch
